method.scope: Broadway plays and musicals that opened from the 2004-2005 season on (seasons run July 1 to June 30). Opening casts only; replacement casting is not counted.
method.classification: Claude (Opus) picked the 1 to 4 headliners of each production from its opening cast and classified their fame as of the opening date. "Film/TV star" is a broad bar: anyone best known to the public from screen work at the time, including regulars of a TV series, not only A-list movie stars. A production counts if any of its headliners qualifies. Every headliner is listed on the page for checking.
method.grossIndex: Average weekly gross over a production's first 16 reported weeks (when the opening cast is usually still in place; some stars leave sooner), divided by the median gross of all Broadway shows that same week (1.00 = a typical show that week). Ticket price and capacity use the same weeks.
method.recoupment: Profitability Scorecard designations. Recouped = Miracle, Windfall, Easy Winner or Trickle. Not recouped = Flop, Fizzle or Did Not Recoup. TBD and tour-stop rows are left out of the recoupment rate, and nonprofit-theater productions are left out of the whole comparison. A show still running counts only once it has recouped or closed, so the rates lean toward finished runs and early hits.
method.classifierReview: Gemini and Codex audited the classifications. Opus re-examined the 44 productions they disputed, under the same rules, and changed 27 of them.
